question: The United Nations has declared 2019 as the____________.

options.text: International Year of Sustainable Tourism for Development

solution:
The correct answer is __**International Year of Indigenous Languages**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The United Nations declared 2019 as the International Year of Indigenous Languages to raise awareness about the critical loss of indigenous languages and the urgent need to preserve, revitalize, and promote them.
 
• The declaration aims to draw attention to the unique role that indigenous languages play in cultural diversity, identity, and heritage.
 
• It underscores the importance of indigenous languages in sustainable development, peace-building, and reconciliation.
 
• The initiative involves various stakeholders including governments, indigenous peoples, UN agencies, and academic institutions to take collaborative actions to support indigenous languages.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indigenous Languages**

 
 
• Indigenous languages are languages that are native to a region and spoken by indigenous peoples. These languages are deeply connected to the culture, traditions, and history of indigenous communities.
 
• Many indigenous languages are at risk of extinction, with estimates suggesting that a language disappears every two weeks.
 
• Revitalizing indigenous languages involves efforts such as language education, documentation, and the use of modern technology to promote their usage among younger generations.
 
• The preservation of indigenous languages is crucial for maintaining cultural diversity and fostering inclusive societies.
 
 
 
• **UNESCO's Role**
 
 
• UNESCO (United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization) plays a pivotal role in advocating for the preservation and promotion of indigenous languages.
 
• UNESCO provides a platform for indigenous peoples to voice their concerns and collaborate on initiatives aimed at protecting their linguistic heritage.
 
• It also supports projects that document and archive indigenous languages, ensuring that they are preserved for future generations.
 
• By promoting multilingual education and integrating indigenous languages into educational systems, UNESCO helps to safeguard these languages and empower indigenous communities.
 
 
 
• **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**
 
 
• The United Nations' Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) include targets that emphasize the importance of cultural and linguistic diversity.
 
• Goal 4 (Quality Education) highlights the need to ensure inclusive and equitable quality education, which includes recognizing the significance of indigenous languages in education systems.
 
• Goal 16 (Peace, Justice, and Strong Institutions) and Goal 10 (Reduced Inequality) also underscore the importance of promoting and protecting the rights of indigenous peoples, including their linguistic rights.
 
• Efforts to revitalize indigenous languages contribute to achieving these global goals by promoting social inclusion, cultural preservation, and educational equity.
 
 
 
• **International Year of Indigenous Languages (IYIL) 2019**
 
 
• The International Year of Indigenous Languages (IYIL) 2019 was a year-long initiative to raise awareness about the critical status of many indigenous languages worldwide.
 
• The initiative encouraged various activities, conferences, and events globally to promote the use, preservation, and revitalization of indigenous languages.
 
• It aimed to foster a greater appreciation and understanding of the linguistic and cultural diversity represented by indigenous languages.
 
• The IYIL 2019 also sought to build partnerships and strengthen cooperation among different stakeholders to support the long-term sustainability of indigenous languages.
